clue.text: Plays outside church in former Greek capital

indicators.note: one thing placed outside another wraps around it, so the plays go round the church

parts.note: plays collectively are drama
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A theatre scene staging plays around a church in Greece's old capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as a city, but here it means money: the DRACHMA was Greece's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital can mean money, and the drachma was the coinage used in Greece until the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Echo and the Bunnymen — do you possess their every last output?

indicators.note: output suggests those letters being put out again in a newly worked order
every last means we keep only the final letter of each word in the stretch that follows

parts.words: and the Bunnymen — do you possess their
parts.note: the closing letter of each of these seven words

explanation.surface: A fan quizzing someone about owning the complete recorded work of the band Echo and the Bunnymen.
explanation.walkthrough: Echo and the Bunnymen is a Liverpool band, so 'Echo' looks welded to the name; it is detached to serve as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To resound is to ring out again with reverberating sound, which is what an echo does as a verb.

clue.text: Moving home, artist's left county

indicators.note: the artist has left, meaning those letters depart from the word for a mobile home

parts.note: a home on wheels that can be towed from place to place
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist moves house and leaves one county behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Caravan is also a Van Morrison song, fitting the puzzle's theme. CAVAN is a county in the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavan is one of the Irish counties, lying just south of the border with Northern Ireland.

clue.text: A day early, put up note of the rainy season

parts.note: Monday, abbreviated, stands for a day
soon means before long, ahead of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so the note's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone posting up a notice a day ahead about the coming wet season.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsoonal is the adjective describing the monsoon, the seasonal wind that brings heavy summer rain to South Asia.

clue.text: One spotted in bad mood, touring

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one word travels all around the other
bad suggests the letters of the following word are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, before being rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recognised while out on a tour, and in a foul temper about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One spotted' sounds like a person noticed, but it is a domino, a tile marked with spots. Domino is also a Van Morrison hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a small playing tile marked with dots or pips, so it is literally a spotted thing.

clue.text: Openings for another one of the 14's group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: entrances that swing open
second meaning: the rock band fronted by Jim Morrison, a different singer of that surname

explanation.walkthrough: 14 is MORRISONS: besides Van Morrison, Jim Morrison sang with the American band The Doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors are entrances in walls, and The Doors were the 1960s rock band led by Jim Morrison.

clue.text: Revolting canned music, starting with old love song

indicators.note: revolting means rising up in rebellion, overturning the order of the letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: starting means we take only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: its opening letter
O is a standard abbreviation for old
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A complaint that piped-in recorded music is disgusting, beginning with some ancient ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old love song' looks like one phrase for the definition, but only 'song' defines: Moondance is Van Morrison's 1970 classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Moondance is a famous Van Morrison track and the title of his 1970 album, so it is a song.

clue.text: No.1 in 9s, when playing a set

definitions.text: No.1 in 9s, when playing a set

indicators.note: number one points to the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: 9s read as nines; its first letter

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being played with and moved about

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing a top tennis player of the seventies in the middle of a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is SEVENTY, so 9s are the seventies. Ilie NASTASE, the Romanian tennis star, was world number one in 1973; the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilie Nastase topped the professional tennis rankings in the 1970s, where he was famous for playing sets with flair.

clue.text: Nothing in opening to Crazy Love that's a surprise

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the others
the opening to a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter
nothing is zero, shaped like O
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone finding nothing remarkable in the start of the song Crazy Love.
explanation.walkthrough: Crazy Love is a Van Morrison song. 'Coo!' is a dated British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo is an informal British exclamation used when something astonishes you, much like 'gosh'.

clue.text: RUC spy arranged a place to meet in Belfast street

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
a venue is where people gather

explanation.surface: A police undercover agent sets up a rendezvous on a Belfast street.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police force. Cyprus Avenue is a Van Morrison song named after the Belfast street.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus Avenue is a real residential road in east Belfast, immortalised in a Van Morrison song.

clue.text: Number of flat in untidy house?

indicators.note: in means one word is put inside the other

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen, used for any filthy dwelling
even means level, as in a flat surface

explanation.surface: Asking a flat's number in a messy house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, but it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy is a cardinal number, the one equal to seven tens.

clue.text: Instruments taking over tenor sax intro

definitions.text: Instruments taking over tenor sax intro

parts.words: Instruments taking over tenor sax intro
parts.note: surface reading: some instruments replacing the saxophone at the start of a track
setter's reading: double-reed woodwinds that could play a passage written for a reed sax

explanation.surface: In an arrangement, a woodwind section takes over the opening bars meant for tenor saxophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are double-reed woodwind instruments, the sort an arranger might hand a saxophone line to.

clue.text: Status taken from group involving a national government funded body

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around, so what is left encloses the next pieces
taken from means that word is removed from the band's full name

parts.note: Status Quo, the long-running British rock band
the word itself, which is removed
taken as written
N is a standard abbreviation for national
G abbreviates government

explanation.surface: A status awarded by a group that includes a national government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Status' looks like a standing; it is the first word of the band name Status Quo.
explanation.definitionFit: A quango is a quasi-autonomous public organisation that receives state money but operates at arm's length from ministers.

clue.text: Net found in Sid Vicious's penultimate appearance in football team

indicators.note: making an appearance in a team means going inside it

parts.note: Real Madrid, the Spanish football club
taken as written

indicators.note: penultimate means last but one, so we keep the second-to-last letter

parts.note: the sixth of its seven letters

explanation.surface: Sex Pistols bassist Sid Vicious making a surprising cameo in a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' means remaining after deductions, as in net profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Net and residual both describe what is left over after everything else has been taken away.

clue.text: Legendary Stones act begins with a mike stand being abused

indicators.note: being abused means mistreated and knocked about, so the letters are jumbled
begins means we take only the first letter of the preceding word

parts.note: its first letter
taken as written
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stones performance opens with the singer mistreating the mic stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' looks like the band; here it is the plural of a mythical stone. The answer also hides Adam Ant, another rock star.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant was a legendary rock or mineral of supposed unbreakable hardness, so adamants are stones of myth.

clue.text: Girl from 3, featuring in Caravan

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within the next word's letters

parts.note: letters four to six

explanation.surface: A girl from an Irish county who appears in the song Caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also inside CAVAN, 3 down, the county the girl comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava is a female given name, as borne by the actress Ava Gardner.

clue.text: Title of today's theme turned up in Berks supermarket

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: berk is British slang for an idiot

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means flipped to read upwards

parts.note: the theme singer was knighted, so his title is Sir

explanation.surface: The name of a singer turning up in a supermarket in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berks' looks like the abbreviation for Berkshire, but it is British slang for fools. The theme is Sir Van Morrison; MORRISONS is a UK supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Morrisons is one of Britain's big grocery chains, founded in Bradford in 1899.

clue.text: Singer in session includes bits of Cleaning Windows?

indicators.note: includes means the phrase before it contains the answer within its run of letters

parts.note: the last letter of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A vocalist in a recording session featuring parts of the song Cleaning Windows.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleaning Windows is a Van Morrison song; read literally, washing glass involves stages of sluicing with water.
explanation.definitionFit: When you wash windows, the bouts of clean water used to sluice off soap are some of the steps of the job.

clue.text: Queen upped the beat, covering 6 — flipping gross!

indicators.note: in a down answer, upped means raised so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: covering means the beat wraps over and around the number

parts.note: a pulse is a regular beat

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the number's numeral is read backwards

parts.note: six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A disgusted reaction to the band Queen speeding up their tempo on a cover version.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' is just the number, not a cross-reference; 'flipping' doubles as a mild British swear word in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross and repulsive both describe something disgusting enough to make you recoil.

clue.text: Today's setter in paper yesterday?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the star that goes down below the horizon each evening
second meaning: a British tabloid that was on sale the day before, as every day

explanation.walkthrough: A setter is a crossword compiler, but also anything that sets in the sky. Today was also a British newspaper, which teases the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The star goes down below the horizon every evening, and a popular British tabloid shares its name.

clue.text: Sort of plane coming from down under, having ejected Unionist Paisley?

indicators.note: having ejected means having thrown out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Down Under is Australia
U abbreviates Unionist
Ian Paisley, the Northern Irish Unionist leader

explanation.surface: An aircraft from Australia that threw out the Northern Ireland politician Paisley.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley led the Democratic Unionist Party in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The astral plane is a mystical realm of existence in occult belief, so astral describes a kind of plane.

clue.text: 9s film shocks cleaner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 1975 Warren Beatty comedy
second meaning: a wash for shocks of hair

explanation.walkthrough: 9s are the seventies, from 9 across. 'Shocks' looks like a verb but means thick heads of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo was a 1975 Hollywood comedy about a hairdresser, and it is also the liquid soap used to wash hair.

clue.text: Fruit given weight by physicist

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A fruit weighed by a scientist, recalling Newton's falling apple.
explanation.walkthrough: The apple suggests Newton, but the physicist is Edward Appleton, who discovered a layer of the ionosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Appleton was a British scientist who won the 1947 Nobel Prize for studying the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: See 8
Some of those blooming old cars don't start — there's one of them in 14!

indicators.note: don't start means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: Morris was a British car maker, its cars being Morrises
surface padding: a thematic aside pointing out that the singular sits inside the theme name

explanation.surface: Grumbling that some of those wretched vintage cars won't start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads as a mild British curse but means flowering. An orris is an iris, and ORRIS sits inside MORRISONS, 14.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a kind of iris, a flowering plant, so orrises are among the plants that bloom.

clue.text: Play a music festival

definitions.meaning: first meaning: freedom of movement, slack
second meaning: an annual festival held in Suffolk, England

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb, but it is a noun for room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means scope or freedom, like play in a rope, and Latitude is a well-known English summer festival.

clue.text: Eyeballs somewhat suave characters when drunk

indicators.note: when drunk means the letters are staggering about, out of their sober order

parts.note: the letters of the word suave

explanation.surface: Smooth people stare at others a little when they have had too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyeballs' looks like a verb meaning stares at; it is the noun, and 'somewhat' says only parts of them are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvea is the pigmented middle layer of the eye, so uveas are parts of eyeballs.

clue.text: Money given to those in debt in Jersey and Guernsey?

parts.note: L is for libra, the pound sign
people who owe

explanation.surface: Cash handed out to debtors in the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey and Guernsey look like the Channel Islands, but they are cattle breeds, and cattle low, or moo.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerseys and Guernseys are dairy cows, and cows low, so they are things that make that sound.

clue.text: No.1 by Kansas, for an indefinitely long time

parts.note: number one is a childish euphemism for urine, as is wee
KS is the US postal code for Kansas

explanation.surface: A chart-topping hit by the rock band Kansas, lasting ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No.1' looks like a hit record, but it is the nursery word for a pee.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something lasted weeks is an idiom for a long, vague stretch, without counting exactly.

clue.text: Be against top model going topless

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, so the first letter is taken off

parts.note: taken as written
to model is to pose for an artist or camera

explanation.surface: Objecting to a supermodel appearing topless.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose something is to resist it or argue against it.

clue.text: All that is offered by Oxbridge poets?

parts.note: Oxford and Cambridge are universities
what poets write

explanation.surface: Wondering if Oxford and Cambridge poets provide everything there is.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the totality of existence, everything that exists anywhere.

clue.text: Get rid of the guitar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cut or dismiss
second meaning: musicians' slang for an electric guitar

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like advice to a band; both halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe is to cut or scrap something, and rock players call their guitar an axe.

clue.text: Session's over — losing heart, as sounds unmusical

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards
losing heart means the central letter is removed

parts.note: the word session

explanation.surface: A band's session is finished, the players have lost heart, and they sound tuneless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like finished, but it turns the word around.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises are sounds lacking tune or harmony, rather than music.

clue.text: Dodgy priests remain

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so the letters cannot be trusted to stay put

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shady clergymen are still around.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue or last on, which is to stay in place.
